policy: Findings CodeQL reports as high or critical in shipped code fail the codeql gate unless one of these entries covers them. An entry covers at most `count` instances of `rule` in `file`; a further instance is a new finding and fails. Every entry has a disposition (false-positive, accepted-risk or tracked-fix), a written justification, an owner, and a review_by date; past that date the check fails until the entry is reviewed again. Adding or changing an entry is a change under .github/ and takes the full Security (SOC 2) and QA gate. See docs/SOC2_CODEQL.md.

entries.justification: The offset advances by snprintf's return only after a guard that the line fits in the remaining buffer, and the call is bounded by sizeof(content) - off, so it cannot pass the end.

browser-lab-build.yml checks out inputs.ref, then runs make and the tests and uses actions/cache, so code from an arbitrary ref can poison caches that default-branch runs restore. One cause; the fix (restore-only caches off the default branch, or a trusted save job) changes the lab build pipeline and is tracked separately.

The HMAC-SHA256 over the password is the SAE hunt-and-peck step IEEE 802.11-2016 12.4.4.2.2 prescribes for group 19, not password storage. The script is a known-answer generator whose only input is the published test PSK 'vector-psk'; it stores and verifies no password. The print of that PSK (the other finding on this file) was removed in code.

The interface name is checked by fl_net_wifi_iface_name_safe (letters, digits, '_', '-', '.', fewer than 16 characters) before it reaches the command; the rest of the command line is constant. CodeQL does not model that check.

CodeQL does not model that check. The program run is always 'iw' from PATH, never a name taken from the environment.

Every value placed in these command lines is quoted or validated: the program path, interface and control directory with shell_single_quote (since this PR), the interface name by fl_net_wifi_iface_name_safe before it is kept, whichever way it was found (environment, nmcli or /proc/net/wireless; since this PR), and the SSID and passphrase by the callers with shell_single_quote or shell_dquote_content; numbers are printed with %d/%u. CodeQL does not model those helpers as sanitizers.

The Wi-Fi host layer runs a helper the process owner names (FL_NET_WIFI_WPA_CLI, FL_NET_WIFI_NMCLI, the Flinstone helper and bridge paths, with the same trust as PATH). That is the intended way to select a Wi-Fi backend. The names are single-quoted, so an environment value cannot add arguments or commands. The environment belongs to the user who runs the shell; nothing here is set by a peer or a letter.

The passphrase has to be in memory to derive the PMK or run SAE; it is never logged or written to a file. The buffer is wiped when the context ends. The SAE context wipes it with fl_net_wifi_crypto_memzero.

The shell runs the program the user typed (exec and the external-command path); that is what a shell is. It runs with the user's own rights and takes the command from the user's terminal or script, not from a peer or a letter.

The path is the file the user names in `server file`, which reads it to offer it to another user. The verbs that read a local file (offer, send -t, log, permit) now run the VM jail and expired-share quarantine check that write uses (since this PR; before it they did not), and read the resolved path that was checked; a path too long to resolve completely is refused. The sharing gate decides who may receive it. CodeQL does not model the jail check.
The path is /sys/bus/usb/devices/<port>/<attribute> for the adapter being probed. Since this PR a port name containing '/' is refused, so the read cannot leave /sys/bus/usb/devices.

The firmware file is the path the operator sets in FL_WIFI_FULLMAC_FW in the process environment (the same trust as PATH); it is read into memory for the adapter and never written. Not set by a peer or a letter.
